name: Determining When a Customer Could Rent a Car (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that determines whether a customer could rent a car based on the inputs that it receives from the car rental agent. Rental cars are available to licensed drivers of 21 years of age or over.
code:
#Step 1: Read the inputs from the car rental agent
text = input("Enter the customer's age:")
age = int(text)
text = input("Enter 1 if the customer has driver's license, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 2: Determine whether the customer has driver's license
if input_num == 1 :
    has_license = True
else:
    has_license = False
#Step 3: Write the boolean expression to determine whether a customer could rent a car
can_rent_car = age >= 21 and has_license
#Step 4: Print the result
if can_rent_car == True :
    print("Yes! The customer could rent a car.")
else:
    print("No! The customer could not rent a car.")

If the customer is exactly 21 and has a license, the expression will be False and the program will deny the rental. That is a problem because someone who is 21 should be allowed. This distractor is plausible because the syntax is correct and the logic looks very similar, but it wrongly excludes an age group you should accept. It does not cause a runtime error, it just implements the wrong age rule.

That means a 20-year-old with a license would be allowed, and a 30-year-old without a license would also be allowed. Both of those are wrong for the rental policy. This distractor is attractive because it uses correct syntax and reads naturally, but it accepts cases that should be rejected and rejects none of the invalid ones tied to the intended rule.

This distractor is syntactically correct and will run, so it can seem plausible, but it flips the license requirement and thus produces the wrong result for every case where the customer actually has a license.
